audit_scope.description: This audit covers EL networking protocol changes (eth/69), CL P2P data column sidecar handling (Fulu/PeerDAS), and EL JSON-RPC configuration exposure (eth_config). Both EL and CL and their interfaces are in scope.

in_scope: P2P Networking (eth/69 handshake, block range tracking, receipt transfer)
out_of_scope: JSON-RPC API general attack surface (out-of-scope per bug bounty)

in_scope: P2P Gossip Validation (data column sidecar validation pipeline)
Peer Discovery (ENR custody fields, supernode thresholds)

out_of_scope_reasons.Mainnet/Testnet Testing: All testing should be done on local forks of testnet or mainnet
out_of_scope_reasons.Pricing Oracles: Incorrect data supplied by third party oracles (oracle manipulation/flash loan attacks are in-scope)
out_of_scope_reasons.Third-party Smart Contracts: Any testing with third-party systems and applications is prohibited
out_of_scope_reasons.Test Files: Impacts on test files and configuration files unless stated otherwise
out_of_scope_reasons.Configuration Files: Impacts on test files and configuration files unless stated otherwise

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer via devp2p (eth/69)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: devp2p eth/69 protocol (Status handshake, BlockRangeUpdate, GetReceipts)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P network peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the network and send arbitrary protocol messages. Peers can lie about their available block ranges, send malformed status messages, or provide corrupted receipt data.

trusted_external_entities.name: Gossip Network Peer via gossipsub
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Gossip peers are unauthenticated P2P participants. They can publish invalid data column sidecars, equivocating sidecars, or flood sidecars with unverifiable proposer indices to exhaust queue buffers.

trusted_external_entities.name: Requesting Peer via CL Req/Resp
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any connected peer can send req/resp requests. Peers can request out-of-range data, send malformed requests, or attempt resource exhaustion by requesting maximum-sized responses repeatedly.

trusted_external_entities.name: discv5 Discovery Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: discv5 ENR records (eth2 fork digest, cgc, nfd fields)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Discovery network is unauthenticated. Peers can advertise false ENR fields including incorrect custody_group_count or fork digest values to manipulate peer selection or eclipse nodes.

trusted_external_entities.name: Local Execution Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Co-located EL client communicates via authenticated Engine API (JWT). However, blob data returned by EL is used without KZG verification—if the EL is compromised or buggy, corrupted data columns will be produced and propagated to the network.

trusted_external_entities.name: Local Validator Set
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Validator balance query for supernode threshold determination
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Local validator configuration is under operator control. The validator balance determines supernode obligations. Misconfigured or manipulated balances could cause a node to incorrectly operate as regular node when it should be a supernode, reducing network data availability.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Client via JSON-RPC (eth_config)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External RPC clients are unauthenticated by default. They can query eth_config for reconnaissance (fork schedule, network configuration) or attempt DDoS via repeated requests. Note: JSON-RPC API is generally out-of-scope per the Ethereum Bug Bounty but is included here for completeness as it affects EL information disclosure.

trusted_external_entities.name: Compromised Node via eth_config Response
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth_config JSON-RPC response (when queried as reference node)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: When a validator queries a remote node's eth_config for configuration comparison, that node could return false configuration data to mislead the validator into accepting incorrect fork parameters.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Must validate networkid, genesis hash, and forkid compatibility. Must handle malformed status messages (missing fields, oversized values). Must enforce timeout on handshake completion to prevent resource exhaustion from slow peers.

Must validate earliestBlock <= latestBlock. Must enforce rate limiting (max once per epoch). Peers may claim false block ranges—node should verify claims when making history requests and penalize dishonest peers.
Must validate receipt data integrity. When receiving receipts without bloom filters (eth/69 format), must correctly recompute bloom filters. Must handle malformed receipt encoding gracefully.

Full 13-step validation pipeline required: structural validity, subnet routing, slot timeliness, finalization check, proposer signature, parent block checks, slot ordering, finalized ancestry, KZG inclusion proof, KZG column proofs, anti-equivocation, and proposer index verification. Each step must be correctly ordered to avoid wasting compute on invalid data.

Must enforce data_column_serve_range bounds. Must enforce MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS response limit. Must order responses by (slot, column_index). Must return ResourceUnavailable (error 3) for out-of-range requests.
Must compute minimum_request_epoch and reject requests for blocks below it. Must only return sidecars that pass gossip validation. Must enforce response size limits.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: discv5 ENR parsing and peer evaluation
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Must validate ENR fields: fork digest compatibility, custody_group_count >= CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT. Must handle missing or malformed cgc/nfd fields. Must not disconnect peers for fork incompatibility before the fork boundary.

EL is trusted for blob content—KZG verification is explicitly skipped for locally-retrieved blobs. If the EL is compromised, invalid data columns will be produced and propagated. The anti-equivocation cache must be updated for locally-imported columns to prevent equivocation bypass via the local EL path.

Combined validator balance must be accurately computed. Balance >= 4096 ETH triggers supernode mode requiring subscription to ALL data column subnets. Incorrect calculation could cause a high-stake validator to under-serve the network.

Must enforce rate limiting (recommended 1 second interval). Should restrict access to trusted interfaces only. Exposes fork schedule and network configuration which could aid targeted attacks. Note: JSON-RPC is out-of-scope per Ethereum Bug Bounty.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: eth_config response consumption (when used for cross-checking)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Configuration data from remote nodes must be cross-checked against multiple sources and the canonical specification. A single malicious reference node should not be able to mislead a validator into accepting incorrect fork parameters.
